summary.headline: SIS Ltd Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 4,816 crore (up 28.1% YoY) and EBITDA a record INR 222 crore, while working capital turned negative.
summary.overview: SIS reported record consolidated revenue of INR 4,816 crore (up 28.1% YoY, 4.6% QoQ) and record EBITDA of INR 222 crore (up 32.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 4.6%, up 16 bps YoY. PAT rose 37.1% YoY to INR 111 crore, the highest in company history. Operating cash flow was negative INR 99 crore on a INR 273 crore working capital outflow, mainly a delayed INR 216 crore collection in Security Solutions International from a large defence client, which management said was received in October. Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.24x from 1.05x in Q1, and management attributed the rise mainly to the international working capital delay.

segments.name: Security Solutions India
segments.commentary: Record revenue INR 2,144 crore (+38.9% YoY, +7% QoQ; 10th straight sequential rise); ex-APS +15.7% YoY. EBITDA record INR 113 crore (+37.2% YoY), margin 5.3% (+16 bps QoQ, flat YoY).

segments.name: Security Solutions International
segments.commentary: Record revenue INR 2,020 crore (+25.7% YoY; +6.3% in constant currency). EBITDA INR 72 crore (+35% YoY), margin 3.6% (+23 bps YoY). Australian wage-linked price pass-through lags due to contract anniversaries.

segments.name: Facility Management Solutions
segments.commentary: Record revenue INR 677 crore and record EBITDA INR 38 crore (ninth consecutive record EBITDA quarter). Margin 5.7%, highest in six years, up almost 50 bps YoY.

segments.name: Cash Logistics (JV, not consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue of about INR 220 crore in the quarter with EBITDA above 17%, per management. SIS holds a minority stake and only its share of profit is reported, under share of profit from JV.

guidance_outlook: Overall revenue growth guidance maintained at 15% to 18%; management said Q2 is in line with it.

India labour-code repricing is at an early stage: India EBITDA grew 13.8% over the six months since June 1; India margin rose from 5.2% in Q4 FY26 to 5.4%. Management expects the margin trend to continue for the next few quarters.
Most of the minimum-wage repricing benefit is still ahead, as enforcement is state-by-state (Karnataka, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand have revised minimum wages so far).
International working capital expected to normalise to about 50 days DSO in Q3; group net debt expected to fall by December.
Management targets debt-to-equity around 1x (currently 1.24x, expected to return to 1x or below) while continuing dividends and buybacks.
Management said FY27 should be one of its better years on a YoY basis.
No India acquisition expected to close in Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Buyback: fifth open-market buyback completed in 45 trading sessions, about 25 lakh shares for INR 106 crore.
Cash Logistics IPO deferred: the approval period has expired; management will revisit at an opportune time.
International acquisitions are being explored in targeted areas (capability, geography, scale); no closure timeline given.
No specific capex or capacity figures were disclosed in the call.
demand_pricing: Labour-code wage increases are being fully passed through to customers, lifting both revenue and margin in India.

Australia: the Fair Work Commission's 4.7% minimum wage increase is passed through at contract anniversaries; bulk falls in July-September and October-December quarters, with a smaller remainder in Q4 and Q1.
Singapore business grew about 20%+ YoY; government grants tied to the wage hike are sunsetting, so EBITDA declined QoQ.
India DSO improved to 73 days from prior levels, and FM DSO was stable at 93 days; international DSO was about 50-51 days in normal cycle.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 290 crore gratuity one-time cost (Q3 FY26) has been recovered, and is there further write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no further write-off; the INR 290 crore was an exceptional item under ICAI guidance. Gratuity paid on separations is being claimed from customers, so no cash impact. A Q4 reversal was an accounting adjustment (liability moved to OCI), not business-related.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue uplift from the minimum wage code be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO gave no numeric estimate. Guidance remains 15-18% overall growth; early repricing is visible with margin up from 5.2% to 5.4%, and the trend is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the policy on dividends and buybacks relative to PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said returns will continue via a mix of dividends and buybacks under the existing policy, alongside investment and debt reduction; no PAT-linked payout figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Cash Logistics IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the approval period has expired; the company will revisit at an opportune time. The business reported record revenue of about INR 220 crore with EBITDA above 17%.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue is at stake in the Australian pass-through, and how is contract repricing timed?
qa_highlights.answer: Murali Krishna said pass-through happens at contract anniversaries, not renewals; bulk falls in Jul-Sep and Oct-Dec quarters. Costs are provisioned ahead, so no loss is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did international working capital deteriorate, and when does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: One large defence client's collection (about AUD/INR 120 million annually per the analyst's figure, confirmed by CFO) was missed at end-September and collected in October. International DSO should return to about 50 days in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the group's sustainable debt level, and what is the cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said India net debt fell to INR 769 crore from INR 796 crore; international net debt rose to INR 256 crore from INR 11 crore. Weighted average cost of debt is about 7.2% (India about 8.5%, international about 6.5%). Target debt-to-equity is about 1x.

qa_highlights.question: What inorganic opportunities are being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: International: targets are being sought for capability, geography or scale, with acquisitions seen as attractive at current multiples. India: focus on solutions-oriented businesses with higher EBITDA margins; nothing expected to close in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Cash Logistics not visible in the reported segment numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is a JV in which SIS holds a minority stake, so it is not consolidated. Only the share of profit appears in the P&L under share of profit from JV; separate disclosure is expected from next quarter.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow of INR 99 crore and working capital outflow of INR 273 crore; the INR 216 crore international collection was received in October and needs to be confirmed in Q3.
Net debt/EBITDA at 1.24x against a stated comfort level of about 1x; management expects a reduction by December.
Wage repricing lag in Australia at contract anniversaries and the Singapore grant sunset, which weighed on EBITDA QoQ.
Pace of state-level labour-code enforcement; most of the India repricing benefit is still to come.
Cash Logistics IPO timing is uncertain after the approval lapsed.
Founder Chairman's passing on 30 October 2026 and Group MD's absence from the call; governance transition is an open question.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, margins and labour-code tailwinds, but cautious and defensive on the working capital and international debt build-up, which management framed as timing. Quantitative guidance on labour-code revenue uplift and dividend/buyback payout was deliberately withheld.
key_quotes: So it means we are not simply getting bigger. We are getting better also as we get bigger.
This is a timing issue, not a credit issue, and the payments, in fact, have already been received in October.
Higher wage and statutory costs are being fully passed through to customers, lifting both the revenue and the margin.
So, we should get back to the usual terms of, the international business roughly hovers about 50 days of DSO, 50, 51 days of DSO, and we should get back to that in the next quarter itself.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance held at 15% to 18%, with Q2 described as in line; backing is labour-code and minimum-wage pass-through in India and Australia plus demand gains, with no capacity additions or orders quantified, so the backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: India margin rose from 5.2% in Q4 FY26 to 5.4% with labour-code repricing at an early stage, management expects the trend to continue, and Security Solutions India EBITDA margin hit 5.3%; Australia pass-through lags at contract anniversaries and Singapore grants are sunsetting, which limits the uplift.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity, plant or branch additions were quantified in the call; capex was not disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Overall FY27 revenue growth guidance held at 15-18% with H1 revenue up about 29% YoY, and organic growth ex-APS was 18.6% in Q2; volume split not disclosed, so the backing is mainly pricing pass-through.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or capacity figures disclosed; utilisation not given, and the call focused on buybacks, debt reduction and acquisitions.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue guidance was merely maintained at 15-18% with Q2 described as in line, and management declined to quantify labour-code revenue uplift.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.24x against a target near 1x and working capital outflow of INR 273 crore needs confirmation in Q3, though the INR 216 crore collection was said to be received in October.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed.

rows.label: International DSO normalises to about 50 days in Q3
rows.why: Management expects international DSO back to about 50 days after the INR 216 crore defence-client collection was received in October, with the INR 273 crore group WC outflow reversing.

rows.label: Group net debt falls by December; D/E back to about 1x
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA is 1.24x versus 1.05x in Q1, and management guided net debt lower by December, with India net debt already down to INR 769 crore from INR 796 crore.

rows.label: State-by-state labour-code minimum wage enforcement
rows.why: Only Karnataka, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand have revised minimum wages so far, and India EBITDA grew 13.8% over six months, so most of the repricing benefit is still ahead.

tone.note: Management was confident on headline growth, India margins and labour-code tailwinds, but defensive on the working capital build and international debt, framing it as timing; analysts pressed on the quantum of the labour-code uplift and the dividend/buyback payout, which management did not quantify.
